skills.name: benchmarking

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. ## Response to Turn 2
2. 
3. ### What I Changed
4. 
5. Applied the `raw-array` `external_body` + `verus_spec` pattern to `alloc`/`alloc_as`
6. exactly as requested, with **one mechanical deviation forced by a Verus front-end
7. panic** (documented below): the abstract view is exposed as a free uninterpreted
8. `bump_view(self)` function instead of an `impl View`/inherent `view()`. It is read by
9. callers identically to `self.view()`.
10. 
11. 1. `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.spec.rs` (~line 158–179) — replaced the attempted
12.    `impl View for FixedSizeBumpAllocator { uninterp spec fn view(&self) -> BumpView; }`
13.    with a free, uninterpreted accessor (the panic-free analog of `raw-array`'s
14.    `uninterp spec fn view(&self) -> Seq<T>`):
15.    ```rust
16.    pub uninterp spec fn bump_view<const N: usize, const A: usize, S: BssStorage>(
17.        a: &FixedSizeBumpAllocator<N, A, S>,
18.    ) -> BumpView;
19.    ```
20.    Also retained (added earlier in this turn during the attempt) the uninterpreted
21.    slot-address accessor, since Verus references — unlike raw pointers — expose no
22.    spec-readable address (`slot as int` fails with `&mut [u8; N]: Copy is not
23.    satisfied`):
24.    ```rust
25.    pub uninterp spec fn slot_ref_addr<T: ?Sized>(r: &T) -> int;
26.    ```
27. 
28. 2. `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs` — `BumpAllocError` enum (~146), `BssStorage`
29.    trait (~191) and `FixedSizeBumpAllocator` struct (~218) carry `#[verus_verify]`
30.    (required so the methods’ `#[verus_spec]` can name the types).
31. 
32. 3. `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::alloc` (~271) — `#[verus_verify(external_body)]`
33.    + `#[verus_spec]`. The `Ok` arm carries alignment + in-bounds over `bump_view(self)`
34.    (not `true`); `Err(_) => true` (the `allocated+1`/uniqueness transition is deferred
35.    to the proving phase per view-design §7, captured by `lemma_alloc_transition`):
36.    ```rust
37.    requires bump_view(self).inv(),
38.    ensures match result {
39.        Ok(slot) => {
40.            let v = bump_view(self);
41.            let a = slot_ref_addr(slot);
42.            &&& a % (v.unit_align as int) == 0
43.            &&& v.base <= a
44.            &&& a + (N as int) <= v.base + (v.storage_size as int)
45.        },
46.        Err(_) => true,
47.    }
48.    ```
49. 
50. 4. `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::alloc_as<T>` (~344) —
51.    `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` + `#[verus_spec]` with the size/align guard arms
52.    and an `Ok` arm carrying `size_of::<T>()==N && align_of::<T>()<=A` plus the same
53.    alignment + in-bounds facts (`vstd::layout::size_of`/`align_of`):
54.    ```rust
55.    requires bump_view(self).inv(),
56.    ensures match result {
57.        Ok(slot) => { /* size_of==N, align_of<=A, aligned, in-bounds over bump_view */ },
58.        Err(BumpAllocError::SizeMismatch)      => vstd::layout::size_of::<T>()  != N as nat,
59.        Err(BumpAllocError::AlignmentMismatch) => vstd::layout::align_of::<T>() >  A as nat,
60.        Err(_) => true,
61.    }
62.    ```
63. 
64. 5. `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md` — registered both functions under "Allowed
65.    `external_body`" with a note that the raw-memory materialization mirrors
66.    `src/libs/raw-array`.
67. 
68. 6. `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-bump-allocator/view_design.md` — updated the View
69.    attachment note to record the `bump_view` free-fn decision and its rationale.
70. 
71. #### Why a free `bump_view` and not `impl view()` (exact error)
72. 
73. I applied the requested `impl ... { uninterp spec fn view(&self) -> BumpView; }`
74. verbatim. The Verus **front end panics** while lowering this `include!`-composed crate
75. (a second `impl` block on `FixedSizeBumpAllocator` collides with the exec-method
76. `impl`). Exact output of `make verify-bump-allocator` with the `impl view()` form:
77. 
78. ```
79. thread 'rustc' (1155145) panicked at vir/src/context.rs:337:13:
80. assertion failed: !trait_impl_map.contains_key(&trait_impl.x.impl_path)
81. note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
82.   process didn't exit successfully: `/home/ruize/toolchain/verus/verus ... --crate-name bump_allocator ...` (exit status: 1)
83.   verification: 0 verified, compilation/setup error (verus did not run) (exit 101)
84. ```
85. 
86. An inherent `impl ... { spec fn view }` form panics identically. The free
87. `bump_view(self)` adds no second impl block, so it lowers cleanly while delivering the
88. same `self.view()` semantics the reviewer asked for (full `BumpView`, `inv()` as
89. `requires`, `base`/`unit_align`/`storage_size` in `ensures`). This is the "paste the
90. exact new Verus error" path the request authorized.
91. 
92. ### Verification
93. 
94. `make verify-bump-allocator`:
95. ```
96. verification results:: 5 verified, 0 errors
97.   Exit code : 0
98.   cheating: assume=0 external_body=2 admit=3 trusted=0 no_decreases=0 cfg_gate=0
99.   coverage: 3/6 exec functions have contracts
100. ```
101. - `coverage-unverified.txt` is now `fmt, new, default` — **`alloc` and `alloc_as` are
102.   gone** (coverage 3/6, target met). `as_mut_ptr` is a body-less trait method, not in
103.   the denominator.
104. - `external_body=2` (justified by the two new `tcb-allowed.md` entries; reported, not
105.   hidden). `admit=3` unchanged (the proof-lemma placeholders; did not grow).
106. 
107. `make verify` (no regressions): every crate exits 0, `0 errors` (kernel: `1 verified,
108. 0 errors`).
109. 
110. `make build` / dual compilation: `cargo build` OK; `cargo test` → 3 unit tests + 1
111. doctest pass.
112. 
113. ### Result: FIXED
114.
